First release. The official Seafile server as one container you can install from a template, on Seafile 14.0.8.

## ✨ Added

- The official `seafileltd/seafile-mc` image, with its own scripts still in charge of setting up, starting and upgrading Seafile. On its own that image expects MariaDB, Redis and the notification server as separate containers on a shared Docker network, plus a JWT key generated by hand. On Unraid that meant several templates, a custom network and a long guide.
- The JWT key, the database password and, if the field is empty, the admin password are generated on the first start and kept in `secrets.env` in the data folder. A value set in the template always wins over the file. The log names a generated admin password once.
- `BUILTIN_MARIADB=true` runs MariaDB 10.11 inside the container, with its data in `/shared/mariadb` and listening only on `127.0.0.1`. The first setup is built in a separate folder and moved into place only when it is complete, so an interrupted first start leaves no half-made database behind.
- `BUILTIN_REDIS=true` runs Redis inside the container as a pure cache, with nothing written to disk.
- `ENABLE_NOTIFICATION_SERVER=true` starts the notification server in the same container and serves it under `/notification`, so the clients see changes when they happen.
- External MariaDB and Redis stay the default, because most Unraid servers already run a MariaDB. The root password is used once to create the databases; with `USE_EXISTING_DB=1` and databases you created yourself it is not needed at all.
- A missing server hostname, database host or Redis host stops the start with one line that says what to set, instead of a Seafile that starts and shows "Page unavailable".
- On shutdown, Seahub and Seafile are stopped before the built-in MariaDB and Redis. The official entrypoint leaves Seafile running until every process is killed.
- `/shared` keeps the layout of the official image, so an existing setup from another Seafile template switches over by pointing the template at the same folder.
- Seafile's own logs go to the container log as well.
- A health check on `/api2/ping/`.
- Images for linux/amd64, the only architecture the official image is built for.

## 🧪 Testing

- Seafile 14 is still labelled testing upstream, so the template is marked beta. Seafile cannot be downgraded: back up the data folder and the database before every update.
- The build starts the image with all built-in services, signs in with the generated admin password, uploads a file, restarts the container and downloads the file again. It also checks that the notification server answers through nginx and that Seafile stops before Redis on shutdown.
